newsitem.title: USA: Hoechst/Schering unit sues Sandoz unit over patent.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst/Schering unit sues Sandoz unit over patent.

text.p: Plant Genetic Systems NV, which is being acquired by the jointly owned AgrEvo crop- protection venture of Hoechst AG and Schering AG, sued Northrup King Co, a unit of Sandoz AG, in a patent dispute.

In papers filed this week in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Plant Genetics alleged that two of its patents for plants genetically engineered to increase their resistance to pests, "transformation vectors...of bacillus thuringiensis," had been infringed by Northrup's sale of plants and seeds "embodying the patented inventions."
Northrup recently received EPA approval for the sale of its insect-resistant corn, which contains a bacillus thuringiensis gene.
Plant Genetic Systems, a privately owned Belgian-Dutch research company, is being acquired for about one billion marks ($673 million).
The lawsuit seeks a court order against further alleged infringement and unspecified damages.
